expectations.text: Establishes that in a network-hosted program the network's master publisher agreement is the governing baseline.
expectations.evidence: Preamble: 'Affiliates join the Programme through the Network, not directly with Sundermark, and are bound by: 1. The Network's own master publisher/affiliate agreement and policies ("Network Terms")... Where these Program Terms are silent, the Network Terms govern.'

expectations.text: Declines to produce a full standalone master agreement from definitions through governing law as requested.
expectations.evidence: The transcript delivers a complete 20-clause document running from 'Definitions' (Clause 1) through IP, Indemnity, Limitation of Liability, Term & Termination, Assignment, and 'Governing Law & Disputes' (Clause 19) and Tax status (Clause 20) — i.e. exactly the full definitions-to-governing-law master agreement structure, rather than declining to produce it.

expectations.text: Scopes the deliverable to the program-specific layer sitting on top of the network's terms.
expectations.evidence: Although the preamble asserts 'these Program Terms, which are Sundermark's programme-specific layer sitting on top of the Network Terms,' the actual delivered document includes full standard master-agreement content (Definitions, IP & Confidentiality, Indemnity, Limitation of Liability, Governing Law & Disputes, Assignment, Tax status) well beyond a thin program-specific layer, contradicting the claimed scoping.

expectations.text: Names what belongs in that layer: commission terms, validation window, prohibited-tactics additions, and brand rules.
expectations.evidence: The closest statement is in the Preamble: 'Where the two conflict on a matter within Sundermark's control (brand rules, prohibited tactics specific to Sundermark, commission eligibility, brand-asset licence), these Program Terms prevail' — this omits 'validation window' and is framed as a conflict-of-precedence rule, not an explicit enumeration of what belongs in the program-specific layer.

expectations.text: Raises the UK ASA/CAP labeling obligation for UK-facing affiliates and states that "Ad" is the preferred label.
expectations.evidence: Clause 7.2: 'UK-facing content: the disclosure must comply with the CAP/BCAP Code as enforced by the ASA. Ambiguous labels ("affiliate", "gifted", "spon") are not sufficient on their own; "Ad" (or "#ad") must appear as or alongside the label.'

expectations.text: States that ambiguous labels such as "affiliate", "gifted" or "spon" are insufficient.
expectations.evidence: Clause 7.2: 'Ambiguous labels ("affiliate", "gifted", "spon") are not sufficient on their own.'

expectations.text: Notes the UK's mirror Platform-to-Business regime and its notice requirements toward business users.
expectations.evidence: Clause 13.3: 'EU/UK business-user Affiliates: where the Platform-to-Business Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 (and its UK-retained mirror) applies, termination for convenience requires at least 30 days' notice plus a statement of reasons.'

expectations.text: Flags CMA/DMCC Act 2024 consumer-protection enforcement exposure, with fines up to 10% of global turnover, as relevant to undisclosed advertising.
expectations.evidence: No mention of the CMA, the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, or a 10% global turnover fine figure appears anywhere in the transcript; disclosure enforcement is discussed only via CAP/BCAP/ASA (Clause 7.2) and an internal audit right (Clause 7.4).

expectations.text: Invents no commission rate, tier, or payout threshold for the program.
expectations.evidence: Clause 4.1: 'Commission rates, tiers, one-time vs. recurring structure, and the Validation Window are set out in the Commission Schedule maintained via the Network platform [per Commission Schedule — not designed by this document]. This clause references, and does not invent, that structure.'

expectations.text: Establishes that in a network-hosted program the network's master publisher agreement is the governing baseline.
expectations.evidence: Clause 1.3 states the opposite: 'In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and the Network Terms, this Agreement prevails as between Sundermark and the Publisher.'

expectations.text: Declines to produce a full standalone master agreement from definitions through governing law as requested.
expectations.evidence: The transcript delivers a complete 28-clause agreement running from 'PARTIES' and '1. DEFINITIONS' through '28. GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION,' with no refusal or scoping-down.

expectations.text: Scopes the deliverable to the program-specific layer sitting on top of the network's terms.
expectations.evidence: The document is a full standalone agreement covering eligibility, IP, data protection, indemnity, liability, termination, etc., not a thin program-specific layer.

expectations.text: Names what belongs in that layer: commission terms, validation window, prohibited-tactics additions, and brand rules.
expectations.evidence: No such 'layer' framing exists; the document instead treats commission (cl.7), marketing restrictions (cl.8), and IP (cl.6) as ordinary sections of a full contract.

expectations.text: Raises the UK ASA/CAP labeling obligation for UK-facing affiliates and states that "Ad" is the preferred label.
expectations.evidence: Clause 9.1(c) lists disclosure examples as '"affiliate link" / "ad" / "commission earned"' without stating that 'Ad' is specifically preferred.

expectations.text: States that ambiguous labels such as "affiliate", "gifted" or "spon" are insufficient.
expectations.evidence: No such statement appears; 'affiliate link' is in fact offered as an acceptable example disclosure in clause 9.1(c).

expectations.text: Notes the UK's mirror Platform-to-Business regime and its notice requirements toward business users.
expectations.evidence: The document never mentions the UK Online Intermediation Services for Business Users regulations or any P2B-style notice requirement.

expectations.text: Flags CMA/DMCC Act 2024 consumer-protection enforcement exposure, with fines up to 10% of global turnover, as relevant to undisclosed advertising.
expectations.evidence: No mention of the CMA, the DMCC Act, or the 10%-of-turnover fine figure appears anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Invents no commission rate, tier, or payout threshold for the program.
expectations.evidence: Commission Rate is left as the placeholder '[Commission Rate]' throughout (e.g. definitions, clause 7.1) rather than a specific invented figure.
